# lean-pkg public-safety

read-only: scan the package's tree and git history for private patterns (exit 1 on hits; publish --yes runs it).

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg public-safety [--history] [--strict] [--package-only] [--gzip-limit BYTES]
                       [--quiet] [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--history, --no-history` | also scan every blob and commit message reachable from any ref (default: on) |
| `--strict` | warn-only hits (latex-label, `warn:` lines) fail the scan too (exit 1) |
| `--package-only` | scan only the package directory even when it is a subdirectory of its repository (default: the whole repository then, which is what promote publishes; the package directory alone is what `release --fresh-repo` exports) |
| `--gzip-limit BYTES` | decode gzip files and blobs (content starting 1f 8b) up to this many decoded bytes each and scan the decoded content (K, M, G suffixes; default: $LEAN_PKG_GZIP_LIMIT, else 512M; 0: no decoding, the compressed bytes are scanned as binary) |
| `--quiet` | only the summary, patterns, warn-only count and verdict lines; no per-hit line (--json is unchanged) |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `public-safety NAME` | read-only: scan what publishing would expose for private strings. The tree is what git would ship (tracked plus untracked, not ignored, files under the package directory); with `--history` (the default) also every blob, every commit message, every author and committer identity (`commit-identity`), every annotated tag (`tag-name`, `tag-identity`, `tag-message`) and every branch and tag name (`ref-name`) reachable from any ref, as lean-pkg's own `make history` does (a blob whose bytes are in the working tree is reported once, as a tree hit). When the package directory is a subdirectory of its git repository, the scan covers the whole repository (tree, every blob, every commit; the summary line ends "scanned the repository root: the package is a subdirectory, and promotion publishes the whole repository"), since promotion makes the whole GitHub repository public; `--package-only` scans the package directory alone (what `repo export` exports). Path-scoped lines stay package-relative and never apply to a file outside the package. A symbolic link is scanned as its target string. Text with a UTF-8/16/32 byte-order mark, and BOM-less UTF-16, is decoded; a line longer than 20000 characters is scanned whole, in overlapping chunks; a binary file is scanned through its printable runs of 4+ characters (hits without a line number); a file or blob is read up to 64 MB. Gzip content (a file or blob whose bytes start with 1f 8b, whatever its name; tree and history alike) is stream-decoded and the decoded content is scanned in place of the compressed bytes (as a stream too: an incremental decoder never cuts a multi-byte character split between two reads, and a long line is scanned in its overlapping chunks as it arrives, so memory is bounded by the chunk sizes, not by the length of a line), whose printable runs only matched patterns by chance: hits carry `encoding: gzip-decoded` and the line number of the decoded text (shown as `path (decoded):LINE`), and the header's original file name and comment are scanned too (`encoding: gzip-header`, `path (gzip header)`). Concatenated members are decoded in turn; zero padding after the last is allowed. A decoded content that is itself binary (a `.tar.gz`: the tar is not unpacked) is scanned through its printable runs and listed in `skipped[]` as `binary (gzip-decoded)`, not blocking. Decoding stops at `--gzip-limit BYTES` decoded bytes per file or blob (`K`, `M`, `G` are powers of 1024; default `$LEAN_PKG_GZIP_LIMIT`, else 512M; a malformed env value is refused; `--gzip-limit 0` turns decoding off and scans the compressed bytes as binary, as before) and when more than 16 MiB are decoded at more than 500 decoded bytes per compressed byte (a decompression bomb). A decode that does not reach the end (`gzip corrupt`, a bad CRC included, `gzip truncated`, `gzip over the N-byte decode limit`, `gzip over the 500:1 compression-ratio guard`) keeps the hits of the part decoded so far, scans the compressed bytes as before and is listed in `skipped[]` with that reason: a blocking `unscanned` hit unless allowed, like any partial scan. Every decoded file or blob is listed in `decoded[]` {where, path, commit (history, when it had a hit), compressed_bytes, decoded_bytes, content `text`/`binary`, complete} and counted on the summary line ("N gzip file(s)/blob(s) decoded"), and printed as a `decoded:` line. Every file or blob not scanned in full is listed in `skipped[]` {where, path, reason, commit (history), unscanned_bytes, allowed} and counted on the summary line ("N file(s)/blob(s) not fully scanned: ..."); a binary one is listed only, any other unscanned portion (past the cap, unreadable) is also a blocking `unscanned` hit unless an `allow:` line applying to the file matches `unscanned` in full (`allow: GLOB: ^unscanned$`). Patterns: the package's `.lean-pkg-private-patterns` (one regular expression per line, `#` comments; a bare line or `block: REGEX` is blocking, `warn: REGEX` is warn-only, `allow: REGEX` lines exempt a matched string; each of the three takes an optional path scope, `allow: GLOB: REGEX`, `block: GLOB: REGEX`, `warn: GLOB: REGEX`, applying only to files whose package-relative path matches GLOB (`*` and `?` within a path segment, `**` across directories; a GLOB without `/` matches the file name at any depth; a trailing `/` matches everything under that directory) and never to commit messages; GLOB is the text before the first colon followed by a space, has no space, colon, backslash or parenthesis, and has at least one of `/ * ? .`, so a plain `allow: https://...` stays global; the file lists private strings, so tracked or in history it is itself a hit and a `WARN`); built-ins `/home/<user>/`, `/Users/<user>/`, `~/Dropbox/`, `approvals/`, `notes/`, `*.private`, `TODO-private`, and email addresses other than the declared ones (the repository's commit and tag addresses that are ordinary mail addresses, `consent[]` entries, `allow:` lines, `example.com`/`.org`/`.net`, GitHub noreply, `git@` SSH remotes; a host-like commit or tag address, one without a dotted domain, `user@hostname`, or under a local TLD, `lan` `local` `localdomain` `localhost` `home` `internal` `intranet` `corp` `private` `test` `invalid` `example`, is not declared by being used and is an `identity-email` hit); user and host names derived at scan time from the record's own `local_path`, `agent`, `workspace` and lease (its `agent`, `workspace` and `contact`; tokens of 4+ characters; never stored; an `allow:` line is matched against the token's whole non-space run and exempts an occurrence only when one of its matches covers it, so allowing a public URL that holds the token leaves the bare token a hit elsewhere); internal files by path (`approvals/`, `notes/`, `drafts/`, `scratch/`, `*.priv`, `*.private`); and the warn-only built-in family `latex-label`, references to a LaTeX manuscript (cross-reference keys `lem:` `thm:` `cor:` `prop:` `def:` `eq:` `sec:` `rem:` `ex:` `fig:` `tab:` `conj:`; the hyphen form only with a digit, a capital or an inner `.` in the label and never for `eq`, `def`, `ex`; never inside a longer name such as `foo_eq_bar` or `Nat.eq:`; built-in allow list `def-eq`, `defeq`, `eq-of`, `eq-iff`, `ex-falso`; `main.tex`; `\ref{` `\eqref{` `\cite{` `\label{` `\input{` `\include{`; `Overleaf`; `arXiv:NNNN.NNNNN`). Each hit has a `severity`: `warn` for `latex-label` and `warn:` lines, `block` for everything else; warn hits print as `WARN` lines. Each hit: location (`path:line`, history adds the introducing commit; commit messages are `commit-message`), a pattern label (a file pattern is labelled `.lean-pkg-private-patterns:LINE`, never by its text) and an excerpt of 40 characters of context with every match replaced by `[…]`: the raw private string is never printed. The summary line ends with how many hits came from `latex-label`. The human report is the summary line, the patterns line and, when there are hits, the verdict line (`ok: ...` or `N blocking hit(s): ...`) up front, then any scan warnings, the blocking hits, the warn-only hits under a `warn-only hit(s): N (families); they do not block` line, and the verdict again as the last line, so a long run of `WARN` lines never hides it; `--json` is unchanged. With no hit and no blocking line in `.lean-pkg-private-patterns` (none, or only `warn:`/`allow:` lines), a `note: no project-specific patterns: built-ins only` line comes before the verdict: 0 hits then means none of the generic patterns matched, not that nothing private is there (see [Before freezing a public candidate](../receipts.md#before-freezing-a-public-candidate)). Exit 0 with no blocking hit (warn hits only), 1 on a blocking hit; `--strict` makes every hit blocking. `--json`: `ok`, `hits[]` (every hit) {where, path, line, pattern, kind, severity, excerpt, commit (history), encoding (gzip content only)}, `tree_hits`, `history_hits`, `block_hits`, `warn_hits`, `latex_label_hits`, `strict`, `history_scanned`, `scope` (`package` or `repository`), `package_prefix`, `skipped[]`, `skipped_blocking`, `decoded[]`, `gzip_limit`, `builtins_only` (true when the patterns file supplies no blocking line), `patterns_source` {file, file_patterns, file_warn_patterns, allow, allow_scoped, scoped_patterns, tracked, builtin[], warn_only[], latex_label_allow[], derived[], internal_paths[], public_allow_file, public_allow}, `warnings[]`. A committed `.lean-pkg-public-allow` at the package root adds `allow:` lines (`allow: REGEX`, `allow: GLOB: REGEX`) that are public on purpose (a fixture address, a generic CI runner path); any other line there is ignored with a warning; inside that file every allow line applies whatever its path scope, and a line a private block pattern matches is the blocking hit `public-allow-private`, which no allow line exempts (tree and history). An address under `.invalid` (or another local TLD) is never declared by being used: it needs an allow line. `--quiet`: only the summary, patterns, note, warn-only count and verdict lines, no per-hit line (exit code and `--json` unchanged) | `[--history\|--no-history]` `[--strict]` `[--package-only]` `[--quiet]` `[--gzip-limit BYTES]` |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

Exit 1 is also a negative answer here:

- `public-safety NAME`: a blocking hit (--strict: any hit)

## JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `public-safety` (exit 0): `block_hits`, `builtins_only`, `decoded`, `gzip_limit`, `history_hits`, `history_scanned`, `hits`, `latex_label_hits`, `name`, `ok`, `package_prefix`, `patterns_source`, `scope`, `skipped`, `skipped_blocking`, `strict`, `tree_hits`, `warn_hits`, `warnings`

## Examples

Scan the tree and the history publishing would expose for private patterns; exit 1 on a blocking hit.

```bash
lean-pkg public-safety my-proof
```
